amendments.rule: A paragogic or cohortative *he*, and a paragogic *nun*, have no English realization and are each their own `unrepresented` unit. These are the bulk of the BSB disagreements in the Psalms, which attaches them to their host word. **The directive or locative *he* is not one of these.** MACULA tags it `Sd`, it carries a motion or a place its host does not, and it takes whatever English the ASV spends on that. Where the ASV writes a word of its own for it — *to*, *unto*, *into*, *toward*, *in*, *upon* — it is its own aligned unit by rule 11 and heads on that word. Where the ASV instead writes a single English word for the host and the *he* together, the two share a unit under rule 30, headed on the morpheme carrying the lexeme: `שָׁמָּה` → *thither*, `הַחוּצָה` → *out*, `הַבַּיְתָה` → *home*, `קֵדְמָה` → *eastward*, `בַּיְתָה` → *inward*, `מַעְלָה` → *upward*, *above*. Mark it `unrepresented` only where the ASV writes nothing for it, which is usually where another morpheme has already taken the English that would have carried the direction, as where `עַד` takes the *to* before a bare place name. Do not reach for this rule's first sentence because the token is a *he*: read the morphology, and where the tag is `Sd` read what the ASV writes.
amendments.why: NUM.26.2, 26.4 and 26.62 all marked the `Sd` of `וָמָעְלָה` unrepresented and all cited rule 32, whose text mentions only the paragogic and cohortative he. Rule 32 is the contract's one sentence about a *he* morpheme, so a verse pass meeting an `Sd` reaches for it; three verses of one chapter did. The corpus decides the case the rule had not considered: of 65 `Sd` units, 19 take *to*, 6 *into*, 4 *toward*, 2 *in*, 2 *unto* as their own aligned units, and every one-English-word rendering of host plus he fuses under rule 30 — GEN.6.16 `מִלְמַעְלָה` → *upward*, 1KI.7.31 `מַעְלָה` → *above*, 1KI.7.11, 1KI.7.25 and 1KI.8.7 the same, with GEN.24.6, GEN.24.29, 1KI.13.7, 1KI.13.15, 1KI.6.15, 1KI.8.8, 1KI.17.3, 1KI.7.39, 1CH.6.78 and JOL.3.11 across the other lexemes; three of those notes say in so many words that the contentful directive he is not rule 32's. The 12 unrepresented `Sd` units are the cases where the ASV writes nothing for it, which the last clause preserves. The one contrary reading is DEU.28.43, whose pair of `מַעְלָה` → *higher* splits host from he; it is two units against roughly fifteen, and this amendment displaces it rather than being contradicted by it. Written as an amendment rather than a new rule so that the over-broad first sentence is corrected where it stands, since that is the sentence a verse pass reads first.

conventions: The directive he of wamaalah shares its host's unit: maalah is one unit rendered upward, headed on maal (rule 30), in 26.2, 26.4 and 26.62. Rule 32 governs the paragogic and cohortative he only and does not reach the locative Sd, which is what the corpus does everywhere the ASV spends one English word on host and he together.

In the clan formula the ASV writes an italic of before a bare name where the Hebrew has no le: 26.5 Hanoch, 26.23 Tola, 26.30 Iezer, 26.31 Asriel and Shechem, 26.32 Shemida and Hepher, and 26.40 of Ard, where both words are supplied. Count the le before placing the of. Where the preposition is written it takes the of; where it is not, the of answers to no morpheme, is its own added unit, and is not folded onto the name or onto the following mishpachat to avoid the added (rules 7, 30).

The enumerated total of the census formula is a verbless clause wherever no hayah stands in it. The supplied were joins the numeral predicate (rule 20) and goes on the numeral the ASV's were stands before, which is the tens numeral in every case here: 26.34, 26.41, 26.43, 26.50. Where a finite hayah is written it takes the were instead (26.7, 26.20, 26.21, 26.40, 26.62), and where the ASV writes no were at all there is nothing to place (26.18, 26.22, 26.25, 26.27, 26.37, 26.47).

ben in the age formula ben esrim shanah is rendered by the ASV's old and takes it: 26.2, 26.4, 26.62. The competing reading marks it unrepresented, but that leaves old licensed by no morpheme, since the numeral and the counted noun have their own English.

report: Cross-verse table: no genuine split. Every multi-treatment bucket is the ASV rendering one morpheme differently in different contexts - le as of/after/according to/unto, et as 'with' at 26.3 (that token is H854, the preposition, not the object marker) against the marker elsewhere, ha as 'that' at 26.10, ki as for/because at 26.62, hayah as were/had/there was/it came to pass. The italic 'of' before a bare name is handled one way throughout: added where no le stands (26.5, 26.23, 26.30, 26.31 x2, 26.32 x2, 26.40), aligned to the preposition where one does. The census copula is placed one way throughout: on the written hayah where there is one (26.7, 26.20, 26.21, 26.40, 26.62), on the numeral the ASV's 'were' stands before where the clause is verbless (26.34, 26.41, 26.43, 26.50).

The real error is not a split - the three verses agree, and agree wrongly. NUM.26.2, 26.4 and 26.62 mark the directive he of wamaalah unrepresented citing rule 32, but rule 32 governs the paragogic and cohortative he, not the locative Sd. The ASV spends one English word, 'upward', on maalah, so host and he share a unit under rule 30. Corpus: GEN.6.16 milmaalah -> 'upward' is one unit of four morphemes; 1KI.7.31 maalah -> 'above', and 1KI.7.11, 1KI.7.25, 1KI.8.7 the same; across the whole Sd set every one-English-word rendering fuses (thither, out, home, eastward, within, without, Jahzah). Two units run the other way, DEU.28.43's pair of maalah -> 'higher', and are the minority reading. Patched all three verses; the fused unit heads on maal and each note names the displaced reading.

BSB disagreements: the three Sd rows are the genuine error above, and BSB is right about them. None of the others is. The six R rows are convention differences the contract already decides - the le of lemor at 26.1, 26.3, 26.52 (rule 27), the resultative hayah le at 26.10 (rule 21), the possessive le at 26.33 and the dative le of 'given them' at 26.62 (rules 40, 43). 26.10's otam is the marker before a suffix whose pronoun the ASV writes once (rule 16). 26.33's suffix has no English because the ASV writes the explicit subject Zelophehad instead of a pronoun (rules 17, 43), and 26.54's two suffixes have none because the ASV writes 'the more inheritance' with no possessive. No accepted edge was changed to improve the aggregate.

Contract: amended rule 32 rather than adding a rule beside it, so that the sentence a verse pass reads first no longer reaches a morpheme it was never about. Four conventions recorded: the maalah fusion, the italic 'of' in the clan formula, where the verbless census copula lands, and ben of the age formula taking 'old'. The gentilic formula mishpachat ha-X-i -> 'the family of the X-ites' is rule 29's own worked example and is not logged again.
